recorded.prompt:q-must-in-cap: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-must-in-cap: P017 survives every cap. It is a must-do project ($`x_{P017} = 1`$), so it always uses one of the $`K`$ allowed outages.
recorded.prompt:q-share: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-share: the plan's count is never negative, so you may multiply both sides by it ... The right-hand side is the count of the *funded* projects, an expression, and not the number of candidates, a constant.
recorded.prompt:q-batches: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-batches: With $`m`$ continuous, the model pays for 1.333 mobilizations, $120k, for 4 projects. The contractor bills whole mobilizations, so the real bill is 2, $180k, and the plan that "fits the budget" overspends it by $60k.

recorded.prompt:q-must-in-cap:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-must-in-cap:b: "It is a must-do project ..., so it always uses one of the $`K`$ allowed outages." The must-do is counted inside the cap, not outside it.
recorded.prompt:q-must-in-cap:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-must-in-cap:c: "If the operator allowed zero outages, the cap row and the must-do row together would allow no plan at all". A conflict arises only when the cap is 0, and caps of 6 down to 3 all solve with P017 funded.
recorded.prompt:q-must-in-cap:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-must-in-cap:d: "P017 survives every cap." The must-do row does not give way.
recorded.prompt:q-share:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-share:a: "The right-hand side is the count of the *funded* projects, an expression, and not the number of candidates, a constant. With 40 candidates, $`0.4 \times 40 = 16`$ would let one region take 16 projects of a 20-project plan, 80% of it."
recorded.prompt:q-share:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-share:b: "A share of an expression is not linear as written ($`\text{count}(S) / \text{count}(P) \le 0.4`$ divides by a variable)"
recorded.prompt:q-share:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-share:d: Applying the page's rule (Reference: "kind $`S`$ is at most a share $`s`$ of the plan | $`\sum_{i \in S} x_i \le s \sum_{i \in P} x_i`$"), the share goes on the plan's count. A count is "the number of funded projects in S", so a count of at most 0.3 allows no Ridge project at all.
recorded.prompt:q-batches:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-batches:a: "a continuous $`m`$ buys fractions of a batch that nobody sells". Only the integer m rounds up.
recorded.prompt:q-batches:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-batches:b: "The row allows any whole $`m`$ with $`3m`$ at least the count." Here 4h >= 5 needs h >= 1.25, so h = 1 breaks the row. Nothing rounds h down.
recorded.prompt:q-batches:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-batches:c: "A mobilization covers up to three vegetation projects" (one hire covers several replacements), and the row is a lower bound that "the cost of $`m`$ keeps ... from rising above what is needed."
